body:
**Blocking - this read-back can't see the change it exists to catch.**

It runs inline and returns `NfcCommandStop`. There's no `NfcCommandReset` first. Compare:

- `:142` - *"Write-mode state machine. Each verify runs after a NfcCommandReset field power-cycle."*
- `:962` and `:985` - both verifies return `NfcCommandReset` before reading the UID back.
- `iso15693_poller.h:65-67` says why: *"a card that only latches the new UID after a reset is not misreported as a failure"*.
- proxmark does the same - `SetTag15693Uid` ends at `switch_off()` and the operator re-runs `getUID`.

This check exists for exactly one scenario: an armed gen1 card whose UID registers at 56/57 get zeroed. That **is** a gen1 UID write by another name - precisely the case the rest of this file says needs a reset before the new UID reads back.

So on gen2 it always passes, which is what your bench measured ("the screen stayed a clean Success"). On gen1 - the only case it's for - it plausibly also passes, having observed nothing. The commit message, the CHANGELOG and the consent-screen comment all now rest on a check that may be a false-negative machine.

Fix is structural: emit the wipe's terminal event from a new state after a `NfcCommandReset`, the way `VerifyGen2` does. That also makes the wipe's verify consistent with the two that are hardware-validated.

**Blocking - the sweep can now cover less than the loop it replaced, and report Success for the gap.**

If a card has a run of >= 8 blocks that answer neither a write nor a read *below* its advertised count, and they don't recover on the re-probe, the sweep breaks here. Everything above is never attempted, `blocks_total` becomes `highest_present + 1`, `failed_count` stays 0 - unqualified Success.

The pre-sweep loop (`block < block_count`, no break) always attempted the whole advertised range. `668f6bc9`'s own message identifies this class and fixes only the half where the blocks recover.

Your reason for not flooring at `advertised` is that a 66-advertised/64-physical card has genuinely absent blocks below its count, and treating those as real reinstates the false "Wiped 64/66, not cleared: 2". Agreed - but those are two separable decisions. *Continuing to sweep* to at least `advertised` and *counting the trailing run as failures* are independent: keep the tail-drop rule exactly as it is, and just don't `break` while `block < advertised`. That restores the old coverage floor at no cost to the fake-flash fix.

Scenario: 64-block card, coupling wobble at block 15 outlasts the re-probe. `wiped = 15`, `blocks_total = 15`, Success. Blocks 15-63 still hold the previous card's data - the same outcome your bench caught, reached a different way.

**Blocking - a truncated sweep and a complete one are indistinguishable to the user.**

`blocks_total` becomes the measured top and the trailing absent run is dropped from the bitmap, so nothing downstream learns the sweep stopped short. The advertised count is right here and is spent on a log line.

Downstream, `nfc_magic_scene_write.c:402` routes a clean wipe to `NfcMagicSceneSuccess`, which is a bare **"Success!"** popup with a 1500ms timeout and no counts at all. So 15-of-64 and 64-of-64 render identically - the user can't tell them apart even in principle.

That's the "unqualified Success" half of the finding your bench confirmed. The mechanism half is genuinely fixed; this half isn't.

I'd deliberately **not** suggest flagging `blocks_total < advertised` as an error - that re-breaks the fake-flash card you tested. What closes it is a qualified success rather than a verdict: give the wipe its own success screen carrying the measured range and the card's claim, e.g. `"Wipe complete / Cleared 64 blocks. / Card claims 64."` Information, no judgement. That makes a truncated sweep visible, and as a bonus a normal wipe finally reports what it did.

The re-probe reads each block into `recheck` and never looks at it - any block that answers is counted via `failed_count += still_absent + 1`.

The main loop 40 lines up classifies a refused write by **content**: read-OK-and-zero means already clear, explicitly *not* a failure. That three-way rule is what `:586-593` documents and what the CHANGELOG describes. The re-probe implements a two-way version of it.

Reachable case: a glitch swallows a block's write ACK *and* its immediate read-back, but the zero-write actually landed. The block enters the absent run, the re-probe reads it back as zeros, and it's reported under "Blocks not cleared" and named in Details - a false Partial where Success is correct.

The same six-line `has_data` scan already exists at `:705-716`; reusing it makes the re-probe agree with the rule the rest of the function follows.

I checked the direction of the error carefully, for what it's worth: the re-probe only ever adds to `failed_count` and raises `highest_present`, so it can't turn a real failure into a clean result. It fails closed. But it manufactures failures for blocks that are fine.

`a2a432f9` added the read-probe, but only inside the `if(!non_empty)` branch. `clone_capacity_confirmed` is still purely positional - `any_failure && wrote_any && !wrote_above_failure` - with no evidence from the card.

And `capacity_confirmed && failed_count > 0` is what prints **"Card too small"** (`nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_write_fail.c:93`), which is the strongest factual claim about the user's hardware anywhere in this feature.

So a persistent top-tail of *non-empty* failures - which is what write-protected or locked upper blocks look like - earns "Card too small" with zero absence evidence. Your own bench log shows it: `oversize_edgedata_70 (non-empty tail, read-back skipped) ... "Not written: 6 / Card too small"`.

That's the same reasoning you applied to the `over_capacity` bucket - *"calling that the card's capacity edge would be a fabricated claim about the user's hardware"* - and it applies verbatim here. The probe is already written and cheap; running it on every persistent failure and letting it gate `capacity_confirmed` would make the claim earned rather than inferred.

`block_size` here comes from `iso15693_3_get_block_size(source)` - a `uint8_t` straight out of a loaded `.nfc`, so 0-255, unclamped - and it's passed as the read length into a 32-byte stack buffer.

The wipe clamps in exactly this situation and says why (`:627-628`, "belt-and-braces"). This new call site doesn't, and the source image is the one geometry input in the whole feature that a user can hand-edit.

Whether it can actually overflow depends on the SDK's rx-buffer handling in `iso15693_3_read_block_response_parse`, which isn't inspectable from the shipped headers - so I can't call it a confirmed overflow. But the asymmetry is new in `a2a432f9` and closing it costs one line.

Separately, same call: the probe uses the **source's** block size rather than the target's. On the gen2 path the CFG frame programs the target to match, so it's fine. On the gen1 path there's no CFG frame, and a mismatch makes the length check fail unconditionally - every empty failure classified as absent, producing a fabricated "Holds X/Y" on a card that holds Y. gen1 is unvalidated anyway, but worth a comment.

No wall-clock bound, and the loop can't be aborted.

A card that answers reads at every address never accumulates `absent_run`, so this runs the full 256 blocks. At your own 40-70ms per refused block, that's a 10-18 second wipe - and because the whole loop runs inside one poller callback, a Back press parks the GUI thread in `nfc_poller_stop` -> `furi_thread_join` for the remainder, with the popup frozen (no progress events are emitted past `advertised`).

Your "Back mid-wipe, view changed 16ms later, no hang" measurement was on a card ending at 64. It doesn't generalise to the ceiling this change introduced - the pre-sweep loop was bounded by the advertised count, so this is new headroom.

A `furi_get_tick()` deadline would do, or resuming from a cursor across callbacks the way `uscuid_ul_poller.c` does. This also interacts with question 1 in your list: whatever we do about Back, the window it has to cover just got longer.

This is the same class of defect `4baf574a` fixed on the screens, still live in the header: an identity claim on a path where the identity may not have been read.

> Wipe: every block the card answered for is clear, and **the UID read back as the one it presented before the wipe**.

`iso15693_poller.c:895-904` sets `uid_changed` **only from a positive observation**. If `verify_inventory` fails all three attempts, the code logs `"wipe: card did not answer the UID read-back"` and falls through - `uid_changed` stays false and Success is returned having verified nothing. Your `.c` comment at `:890-894` states that rule explicitly and correctly; this line states the opposite as fact.

Suggested: *"...and the post-wipe UID read-back did not come back different (a read-back that fails outright is logged and does not block Success)."*

Secondary, same sentence: "is clear" is an ACK-level claim - blocks that accept the zero-write are never read back - which contradicts the clone caveat two lines above it ("a data block counts as written when the card ACKs it").

This still carries the proxmark claim you corrected everywhere else this round.

> write zeros to every data block the card PHYSICALLY holds, **like proxmark's 'hf 15 wipe'**

`CmdHF15Wipe` sweeps blindly and `break`s at the first refusal, and there's no `GET_SYSTEM_INFO` call anywhere in it. Writing every block the card physically holds is precisely the behaviour **this PR added and proxmark lacks** - which is what makes the sweep worth having.

`iso15693_poller.c:97-99` already concedes this ("proxmark breaks at the FIRST refused write... the tolerance below is ours, not its precedent") and `f31c2f34` corrected the CHANGELOG. The header contradicts both, in the same PR.

Dropping `, like proxmark's 'hf 15 wipe'` is enough. The one proxmark parallel that does survive is the write order, and `:643-644` states that correctly.

The wipe-mode definition is now incomplete, and it feeds a number the user reads.

> In wipe mode, blocks that still held data after a failed zero-write.

The sweep also folds **interior absent blocks** into `clone_failed_count` at three sites - `:682`, `:700` and `:758` (`+= absent_run`, `+= still_absent + 1`). Those blocks answered *nothing*; they demonstrably did not "still hold data".

This reaches the screen: `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_write_fail.c:79` prints `"Not cleared: %u"` from it, and the Details list names their indices. Drift introduced by the sweep rework that neither this doc nor its twin at `iso15693_poller.c:170-173` caught up with.

Suggested: *"wipe: blocks not shown to be clear - either they answered a read and still held data, or they answered nothing at all with a block above them that did (interior fault, failed closed)."*

> the scene doesn't have to know that the gen1 frames go out unconditionally at Start

They don't. `write_step`'s `Start` case has two `return NfcCommandStop` paths above the gen1 send: `:928-933` (`uid_unverifiable`) and `:938-944` (empty clone source). Both leave `gen1_attempted == true` with zero frames sent.

The `uid_unverifiable` path is safe because the scene's reason ladder checks it first. The empty-source-gen1-clone path would route to `Gen1Failed` and tell the user "56/57/62/63 may be overwritten" about a card nothing touched - **currently unreachable through the UI**, since the gen2 run hits the same empty-source guard and Fails before `NotGen2` can offer gen1.

So: no live user impact, but `iso15693_poller_start_clone_gen1()` is public API and this comment is what a future caller would rely on. Same claim at `iso15693_poller.h:174`.

My overclaim, my correction: **nothing documents that ordering.**

proxmark's `SetTag15693Uid` sends `0x3E`, `0x3F`, `0x38`, `0x39` with no explanatory comment; `doc/magic_cards_notes.md`'s ISO15693-magic section has `**TODO**` for its entire body; and *unlock*, *arm*, *commit*, *de-arm* appear nowhere in an ISO15693 context in that tree. It's one implementation's observed order, and `hf_15_magic.lua` copies it.

Suggested: *"the reverse of the only ordering anyone has been observed to use (proxmark3 `armsrc/iso15693.c:3191-3200`; neither it nor `hf_15_magic.lua` documents why)."*

Same root at `:26-27`: `BLK_UNLOCK` / `BLK_COMMIT` and "arms the UID change" are our inference from the write order - proxmark asserts neither the names nor the semantics. Worth marking as inference, because the whole OPEN QUESTION and the wipe's UID hazard rest on that reading being right.

The conclusion isn't affected. Your framing - there's no safe order because the only route to the latch is the sequence that sets it - holds regardless.

This is the most valuable comment in the feature and I'd like it to survive, so: four of the symbols it and its neighbours cite aren't in the shipped SDK.

- `VIEW_DISPATCHER_QUEUE_LEN` - zero matches in `sdk_headers/f7_sdk`; `view_dispatcher_i.h` doesn't ship, so the 16 isn't checkable from an app.
- `view_dispatcher_send_custom_event` "blocks with `FuriWaitForever`" - the function is public, that property isn't documented anywhere in the header.
- `iso15693_3_poller_filter_error` (`:690`) - not exported; static in the firmware tree.
- `iso15693_3_write_block_response_parse` (`:330`) - not exported either.

All four claims are, as far as I can tell, **true** - they're just unverifiable from where this code sits. The risk is a maintainer greps the SDK, finds nothing, concludes the deadlock argument is stale and raises the bound.

Re-attributing rather than deleting: *"(observed in the firmware source at <path>; not visible in the shipped SDK headers, so it can't be asserted from the app side)"*.

While here, `:54-57`: 40 x ~100ms is 4s, not the "5-7 second timeout" the same comment concludes, and no ~100ms constant exists under `lib/nfc` in the headers. Either state the measured wall-clock and drop the derivation, or fix the arithmetic - but not both.

This retry loop is character-identical to the clone's at `:483-488`, modulo the data pointer and size.

That duplication is why `a55ce29c` exists. The wipe's copy had drifted to retry only past the cap, silently leaving blocks unwiped, and the fix was to bring it back into line - which is the failure mode a shared helper makes structurally impossible.

Three more primitives are duplicated the same way:
- is-buffer-all-zero: `:503-509`, `:705-711`, `:1285-1287`
- bitmap set/clear: `:501`, `:715`, `:723`, `:780`
- "block answered, so absences below it are interior faults": `:681-686`, `:700-704`, `:758-761` - three copies inside `wipe_blocks` alone

One `iso15693_write_block_retried()` plus `iso15693_block_is_empty()` would be ~15 lines and behaviour-preserving by construction.

I'd put this in a separate pass from the blocking items, not the same one - but of everything in the simplification list this is the piece I'd treat as non-optional, because it has already cost a shipped bug once.

This file is up to **10 render branches**, and five of them are byte-identical in shape - a title plus a constant three-line body at `(0,13)`, differing only in two string literals: `nothing_wiped`, `nothing_cloned`, `gen1_failed`, `uid_unverifiable`, `empty_source`.

A file-static `{reason, title, body}` table plus one render call collapses ~71 lines to ~22, leaves `over_capacity` / `partial` / `wipe_uid_changed` / `uid_unexpected` as the branches that genuinely compute their text, and lets a `switch` give you `-Wswitch` coverage over `NfcMagicIso15693WriteFailReason` - so a new reason can't silently fall through to "Not a magic tag" the way one could before.

Also in this file: the "two 4-byte groups, unspaced, because the spaced form overruns 128px" UID hex loop is written twice (`:155-158`, `:173-178`) - worth extracting so that layout constraint lives in one place, given the reflow commit exists precisely because these bodies overran their space.

Separately, `scenes/nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_write_confirm.c` (68 lines) is character-for-character identical to the shared `nfc_magic_scene_write_confirm.c` except for two strings, a button label and the text-box height - it could fold into the shared scene the way the ISO15693 wipe branch already does.

This still describes the wipe-failure screen as saying **"and the UID is unchanged"** - which `4baf574a` deleted from that screen, correctly, because nothing reads the UID on that path (the re-read is gated on `wiped > 0`).

So the user-facing changelog now over-claims where the screen no longer does.

Suggested: *"a wipe failure saying no block accepted the zero-write"*.

The comment above that string in `nfc_magic_scene_iso15693_write_fail.c:105-107` has the same problem - it still instructs the string to "say so" about the UID, describing the pre-`4baf574a` text.
